title: GPU Fleet Capacity, Terraform/IaC and CI/CD Runbook (2026 ops)
author: Daniel Park
body:
Summary:

This runbook documents operational run procedures for Redwood Inference's GPU fleet capacity, Terraform/IaC modules, and CI/CD build pipelines used to provision and operate inference capacity. It is intended for on-call infra engineers, SREs, and platform engineers who execute day-2 operations, incident response, and planned maintenance.

Scope:

- Services covered: gpu-provisioner (control plane), capacity-manager (autoscaling controller), node-bootstrap (image/agent), and the IaC modules under modules/gpu-* in the infra repo.
- Cloud accounts: aws-prod (primary), aws-staging, gce-prod (experimental).
- Activities: capacity scaling, replenishment, rolling upgrades of GPU hosts, Terraform apply and rollback, CI/CD failures, and capacity-related incidents.

Owners and Contacts:

- Primary owner: infra/compute team (oncall alias: infra-compute-oncall@redwood.example.com)
- Secondary: eng-sre (sre-oncall@redwood.example.com)
- Pager escalation: 15m -> oncall lead, 30m -> infra manager, 60m -> CTO on call.
- Slack channels: #infra-ops, #gpu-fleet-alerts.

SLOs and Operational Targets:

- Capacity availability SLO: 99.95% across regions for provisioned capacity (measured per 24h).
- Provisioning latency target: new GPU host ready for scheduling within 10 minutes 95th percentile.
- Autoscaler correctness: target <1% failed scale actions per day.
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - PendingPodBacklog > 50 for > 5m -> P1 alert (scale/evacuate).
  - HostProvisionFailure rate > 5% in 15m -> P1.
  - Terraform apply error rate > 3 consecutive failures -> P2.

Capacity Model and Policy:

- Baseline committed capacity is defined in terraform/terraform.tfvars per account. Burstable capacity is available via spot/interruptible pools with graceful fallbacks to on-demand.
- Pools: inference-hot (low-latency, A100/4090), inference-warm (throughput), batch (spot).
- Autoscaling: capacity-manager watches queue depth and per-model qps; scale up uses on-demand, scale down prefers draining spot first.

Terraform / IaC modules and repo layout (high-level):

- repo: infra/ (gitlab)
  - modules/gpu-instance: module to create instance+ebs+nv_peer_iptables
  - modules/gpu-asg: ASG with mixed instances for spot/on-demand
  - modules/gpu-networking: VPC subnets, ENI attachment policy, SGs for RDMA and control plane
  - live/prod/gpu-fleet: composition + var files
- Key module variables to watch: gpu_type, desired_capacity, spot_percentage, drain_grace_seconds, instance_role_arn.
- When modifying modules: always bump module version tag and run terraform plan in staging before prod.

CI/CD and Build Pipelines:

- Pipelines: infra-ci (lint/terraform-validate), infra-apply (staging), infra-apply-prod (manual gated)
- Build artifacts: AMI bake pipeline (packer), node-agent image (container registry), kernel/driver package versions tracked in versions/gpu-ami.yaml
- Gate checks: terraform fmt, tflint, terratest for critical modules (gpu-asg), security-scan.
- Manual approval required for any change that updates desired_capacity or changes gpu_type in prod.

Key Dashboards and Alerts:

- Dashboards: GPU Fleet Overview (Grafana), Host Provisioning Latency, Pending Pod Backlog, Node Draining Progress.
- Pager alerts: configured in PagerDuty integration; their runbooks should be referenced from the alert description (link to alert rule id in related_pages).

Runbook: Common Incidents and Playbooks:

1) Partial capacity depletion (spot eviction surge) - P1

- Symptoms: sudden drop in available GPU hosts, increase in PendingPodBacklog, many pods in Pending (InsufficientGPU).
- Immediate actions (0-10m):
  1. Acknowledge PagerDuty, post incident header in #gpu-fleet-alerts with current counts.
  2. Check Grafana panels: PendingPodBacklog, HostCount by pool, SpotEvictionRate.
  3. If spot eviction > 10% of pool size: scale up on-demand pool by +20% (see Terraform quick action below) or enable burst buffer quota.
- Mitigation (10-30m):
  1. Run: git checkout live/prod/gpu-fleet && terraform plan -var='desired_capacity=NEW' -var='gpu_type=ON_DEMAND' -out=plan.out\ 2. Apply after review: terraform apply plan.out (infra-apply-prod pipeline preferred).
  2. If Terraform apply is blocked, increase capacity via cloud console as emergency (document change after).
- Post-incident (after stabilized):
  1. Create postmortem if impact > 1 hour or > 5% customers affected.
  2. Re-evaluate spot percentage and fallback policies.

2) Failed Terraform apply in prod (module change causing drift) - P2

- Symptoms: infra-apply-prod job fails with validation/apply errors, partial infrastructure changes, or plan shows unexpected deletions.
- Steps:
  1. Do NOT re-run apply. Capture Terraform state and plan output.
  2. If plan shows destructive changes, pause pipeline and escalate to module owners.
  3. Run terraform state pull and save a copy to S3 bucket infra-state-backups/YYYYMMDD-HHMM.
  4. If safe, roll back by restoring previous state: terraform state replace-provider or use state restore procedure (refer to state restore checklist).
  5. In severe cases, open an incident and notify platform leads.

3) Host image (AMI) regression after bake (drivers/Kernels) - P1

- Symptoms: node_bootstrap failures, GPU drivers failing to load, increased HostProvisionFailure or node crash loops.
- Steps:
  1. Isolate by pausing the AMI bake pipeline and reverting artifacts in the registry.
  2. Mark the AMI as deprecated in versions/gpu-ami.yaml and re-run prerelease tests on staging.
  3. If nodes are unhealthy, cordon and drain affected nodes and scale up unaffected AMI pool.

Runbook: Emergency Terraform quick actions (when CI/CD is unavailable):

- Quick manual change (EMERGENCY ONLY):
  1. Create an emergency change ticket and get approval from oncall lead.
  2. In the cloud console, adjust ASG desired capacity for inference-hot / inference-warm.
  3. After change, run terraform import to align state: terraform import module.gpu-asg.aws_autoscaling_group.this <asg-id>
  4. Add a remediation commit to the infra repo and trigger infra-apply-prod once CI returns.

Day-2 Ops and Maintenance Tasks:

- Weekly: review used GPU types and spot utilization; reconcile desired_capacity with observed baseline.
- Monthly: AMI bake and driver patching window (first Saturday 02:00-06:00 UTC).
- Quarterly: capacity stress test (simulate 2x load for 2 hours) and review autoscaler thresholds.
- Runbook drills: game-day exercises twice per year (owner: eng-sre).

Rollout checklist for new GPU instance types (e.g., new A100 variant):

1. Create module change: add supported_instance_types var and defaults.
2. Bake AMI with drivers and run terratest suite (smoke, perf).
3. Stage rollout: bring up a small pool in staging, run production-like workloads.
4. Canary in prod: add 5% of traffic to new instance pool, monitor tail latency and error rate for 24h.
5. Full rollout: if canary OK, update desired_capacity and deprecate legacy types.
6. Document capacity delta and cost impact in the release note.

Operational tooling and useful commands:

- Terraform plan in staging: cd infra/live/staging/gpu-fleet && terraform init && terraform plan -var-file=staging.tfvars\- Terraform apply prod (manual gate): run via infra-apply-prod pipeline URL or run locally only with manager approval.
- Import ASG after console change: terraform import module.gpu-asg.aws_autoscaling_group.this <asg-id>
- Check host provisioning logs: kubectl -n kube-system logs daemonset/node-bootstrap -l app=node-bootstrap --since=1h\- List pending pods: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide | grep Pending

Post-incident and Change Management:

- All emergency manual changes must be followed by a remediation PR within 24 hours that brings Terraform state back in sync.
- For any capacity-impacting change, schedule a rollback window and notify customer-success for enterprise customers.
- Postmortems: follow the incident-process template; include timeline, root cause, mitigation, action items and owners.

Appendix: Troubleshooting Matrix (short)

- Symptom: PendingPodBacklog -> Check node availability, daemonset logs, kube-scheduler logs, then autoscaler metrics.
- Symptom: HostProvisionFailure -> Check AMI bake status, cloud-init logs from instance console, and driver install logs.
- Symptom: Terraform unexpected deletions -> Stop pipeline, save state, run terratest locally, escalate.

- Team playbook: confluence/eng-infra/team-wiki/infra-gpu-fleet-capacity-ci-cd-iac-playbook-2026
